title: Beach Hazards Statement
location: Coastal Onslow

details.description:
* WHAT...Strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Onslow County beaches.

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.
details.instruction:
Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

details.description:

* WHERE...For the dangerous rip currents, the beaches from Cape

strong longshore currents in the surf zone, the beaches from
Cape Hatteras to Bogue Inlet

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Strong longshore currents will
create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 7:30 AM and 8:40 PM.
details.instruction:
Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

title: Extreme Heat Watch
location: Kofa; Central La Paz; Southeast Yuma County; Gila River Valley; Joshua Tree NP West; Joshua Tree NP East

details.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible. Afternoon temperatures
108 to 116. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...In Arizona, Central La Paz, Gila River Valley, Kofa, and
Southeast Yuma County. In California, Joshua Tree National Park.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
details.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Watch means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, may occur. Actions should be taken to lessen
the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

title: Special Weather Statement
location: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Western Capes

details.description:
A series of strong Bering Sea systems will bring widespread
moderate to heavy rain at times along gusty winds and rough seas
for the coastal waters. Here is what to expect from each system:

Tuesday:

-Winds: Southeast winds of 20 to 30 mph with gusts of 35 to 40
mph along the Kuskokwim Delta Coast early Tuesday morning through
late Tuesday morning. Gusts up to 45 mph are possible around
Cape Newenham. Winds slowly diminish beginning late Tuesday
morning.

-Wave Heights: Expect rough seas near the coast with wave heights
of 7 to 10 ft likely. Highest waves will be around Cape Newenham
and into Etolin Strait. Wave heights slowly subside beginning
late Tuesday morning.

-Rainfall amounts: Expect steady light rain (about 0.25 to 0.50
inches storm total), with highest totals by Cape Newenham.


Wednesday into Thursday:

-Winds: Southerly to southwest winds up to 35 mph with gusts up to
45 mph. Winds slowly diminish through Thursday morning.

-Wave Heights: 5 foot waves Wednesday morning build to 8 to 11 ft
Wednesday afternoon. Wave heights slowly subside beginning
Thursday morning.

-Rainfall amounts: Expect moderate to heavy rain at times (about
0.50 to 1.00 inches storm total), with the highest amounts near
Quinhagak and Platinum.

title: Special Weather Statement
location: Northern Bristol Bay Coast

details.description:
A series of strong Bering Sea systems will bring moderate to
heavy rain at times along the coast as well as gusty winds and
rough seas along the coast waters of Northern Bristol Bay. A
southerly push of winds up Nushagak Bay both Tuesday morning and
Wednesday morning may bring increased water-levels up the Bay but
coastal flooding is of little to no concern due to lower tides.
Here is what to expect from each system:

Tuesday:

-Winds: Southeast winds 20 to 25 mph Tuesday morning with gusts
up to 30 mph.

-Wave Heights: Expect peak wave heights of 6 to 10 feet along
coastal Bristol Bay by Tuesday afternoon. These elevated wave
heights will persist through the rest of Tuesday with the
southwesterly fetch.


-Rainfall accumulations: Expect moderate to heavy rain at times
(about 0.75 to 1.25 inches storm total), with the highest totals
towards the Nushagak Peninsula/Cape Constantine.


Wednesday into Thursday:

-Winds: Southerly winds in the morning turning southwesterly
through the day and increasing to 25 to 35 mph. Gusts between 35
to 45 mph. Peak winds occur Wednesday afternoon into Wednesday
evening before slowly diminishing through Thursday morning.

-Wave Heights: Expect peak wave heights of 9 to 13 ft Wednesday
afternoon to Wednesday evening for the coastal waters of northern
Bristol Bay. Wave heights begin to slowly subside through
Thursday morning.

-Rainfall amounts: Expect a steady light rain (about 0.50 to 0.75
inches storm total), with the highest totals near Togiak.

title: Heat Advisory
location: Clinton; Washington; Randolph; Madison; St. Clair; Monroe; Boone; Moniteau; Cole; Osage; Callaway; Montgomery; Gasconade; Warren; St. Charles; Franklin; St. Louis; St. Louis City; Jefferson; Crawford; Washington; St. Francois; Ste. Genevieve; Iron; Madison; Reynolds

details.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values of 100 to 110 degrees.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Illinois and
central, east central, and southeast Missouri.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This is the fourth straight day with heat
index values of 100 degrees or higher over parts of the area.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances. Take extra precautions if you work or spend time
outside. When possible reschedule strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion
and heat stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when
possible. To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety
and Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks
in shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.
